extracted.intended_audience: PIs and senior personnel preparing NIH grant biosketches for NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing the NIH Biosketch sections: Personal Statement (Section A) and Contributions to Science (Section C), including length limits, content, style, and citation rules for applicants at different career stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement — length limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SciENcv to complete the biosketch; ensure the entire personal statement, including spaces, fits within the 3,500-character limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement — purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your case for why you are well-suited to your role on the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include key aspects of training or past experience, technical expertise, significant collaborations, past performance in this or related fields, and an opportunity to explain anything else you'd like reviewers to know about your career and research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement — style
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in the first person and tailor the statement to each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use I/me/my/we; do not submit a generic statement across applications; explicitly address career interruptions, transitions, or special circumstances when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Statement — content guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Core content elements to include in the personal statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your role on the project; highlight expertise relevant to the proposed work; cite key papers (NOT as formal references — refer to publications/products in 'Other Significant Products'); mention awards and leadership roles; explain your career trajectory if non-traditional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science — number and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe up to five of your most significant contributions to science; each contribution is limited to 2,000 characters (including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select up to five contributions and ensure each description (including spaces) stays within the 2,000-character cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science — strategy by career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested number/depth of contributions depending on career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate students and postdocs: highlight two or three significant contributions; mid-career: three to four well-developed contributions; senior investigators: use all five to demonstrate breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to Science — format for each contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contribution should include a brief description covering historical background, central finding(s), influence on the progression of the field, and your specific role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure each contribution as a short narrative that situates the work historically, summarizes key findings, explains impact on the field, and clearly states your personal role in the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and references policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You may NOT include references in Contributions to Science or Personal Statement; instead, refer to publications/products selected for the 'Other Significant Products' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insert formal reference lists in these sections; instead, identify (by short citation labels) up to four supporting publications per contribution via the 'Other Significant Products' entries. Each contribution can cite up to 4 supporting publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers tend to base expectations on an individual's seniority and expect relevance and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on accomplishments and expertise directly relevant to the proposed work; emphasize quality over quantity; craft a narrative that communicates your scientific identity and how past work connects to the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common mistakes to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent errors applicants make in Personal Statement and Contributions to Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid generic personal statements not tailored to the project; avoid listing too many publications (low signal-to-noise); do not list every paper rather than synthesizing contributions; clearly explain your specific role in collaborative work; ensure you explicitly connect past work to the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 2026 NIH Common Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the updated NIH Biosketch Common Form (required for due dates on or after January 25, 2026) and submit via SciENcv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of format changes and updated instructions (including demographics and identity fields) in the 2026 Common Forms version; SciENcv must be used to complete and submit the biosketch.
